scenarios.name: Power out for three days in winter
scenarios.setting: A winter storm brings down power lines. The power goes out at dinner time, and the news says it may be out for three days. It is cold outside.

prompts.ask: The lights just went out. What do you do first?
ready: Flashlights or battery lanterns where everyone can find them in the dark
Everyone knows to use flashlights, not candles, when the power is out
A way to check that everyone at home is safe
Everyone knows to keep the fridge and freezer shut
prompts.fix: Flashlights where everyone can find them in the dark

prompts.ask: How does everyone stay warm tonight?
ready: Warm clothes, blankets or sleeping bags for everyone
A plan to keep everyone warm in one room
Everyone knows a grill, camp stove or generator is never used indoors or in a garage
Everyone knows a generator stays outside, well away from windows, doors and vents
Everyone knows the oven is never used to heat the home
A carbon monoxide alarm that works on batteries, tested
prompts.fix: A way to keep warm with no power, and a carbon monoxide alarm that works on batteries

prompts.ask: Power lines are down in the street. How do you get news and keep phones working?
ready: Stay well away from downed lines and anything touching them, and keep others away. Treat every line as live. Report it.
A radio that runs on batteries or a crank
Power banks that are kept charged
Everyone knows to use phones only when needed
prompts.fix: A radio that needs no power, charged power banks, and everyone knows to stay away from downed lines

prompts.ask: What do you eat and drink?
ready: Food that needs no cooking and no fridge
A can opener that works by hand
Stored drinking water
A plan to eat food from the fridge first
prompts.fix: Food that needs no cooking, a hand can opener and stored water

prompts.ask: Someone at home has medicine that must stay cold, or a device that needs power. What now?
ready: A list of who needs cold medicine or powered devices
A plan for keeping medicine cold, or where to take it
Knowing somewhere nearby with power, like a public warming place
The pharmacy or doctor's number on paper
prompts.fix: A plan for medicines and devices that need cold or power

prompts.ask: The pipes might freeze. What do you do?
ready: Everyone knows where the water shutoff is
Knowing to open cupboard doors under sinks so warmer air reaches the pipes
Knowing to follow local advice about leaving taps dripping
A number to call for a burst pipe
prompts.fix: Know where the water shutoff is and how to turn it off

prompts.ask: A neighbour who lives alone has not been seen today. What do you do?
ready: Someone who can check on them safely, in daylight
A way to reach their family
Knowing when to call for help
prompts.fix: A way to check on neighbours who live alone

prompts.ask: The power comes back. What do you check?
ready: Everyone knows that food which got warm is thrown out when in doubt
Knowing to turn appliances back on one at a time
A plan to replace the batteries, water and food that were used
A talk about what went well and what to fix
prompts.fix: Restock what was used after an outage

scenarios.name: A storm with flooding and an order to leave
scenarios.setting: It has rained hard for two days and the river is rising. Local officials order your area to leave within two hours.

prompts.ask: How did you hear the order, and how do you know it is real?
ready: Emergency alerts turned on on the phones
A radio
Knowing the official local source to check
prompts.fix: Emergency alerts turned on, and an official source to check

prompts.ask: Who does what right now?
ready: Each person has a job: pets, papers, bags, the car
Everyone knows the meeting place
Someone knows to tell the out-of-area contact
prompts.fix: A job for each person when the household must leave fast

prompts.ask: What do you take?
ready: Go-bags packed and ready
Medicines and glasses
Important papers or copies of them
Phone chargers and some cash
Pet food, leads and carriers
prompts.fix: Go-bags packed, with medicines, papers, chargers and cash

prompts.ask: What do you do to the home before you leave?
ready: Someone knows how to turn off the power and water, and knows to do it only if officials say so and it is safe, never while standing in water or wet
Doors locked
prompts.fix: Know how and when to turn off the power and water

prompts.ask: There is water across the road ahead. What do you do?
ready: Everyone knows never to drive or walk into flood water
Everyone knows to turn around and take another way
Two ways out of the area known ahead
prompts.fix: Two ways out of the area, and the rule never to drive into flood water

prompts.ask: Where do you stay tonight?
ready: A place outside the area agreed ahead
Knowing where official shelters are announced
A place for the pets too
prompts.fix: Somewhere to stay outside the area, pets included

prompts.ask: Someone in the household is not with you. How do you find each other?
ready: An out-of-area contact everyone checks in with
Numbers written on paper, not only in phones
Everyone knows to send texts rather than call when lines are busy
prompts.fix: An out-of-area contact, and numbers written on paper

scenarios.name: A wildfire smoke week
scenarios.setting: A large fire far away fills the air with smoke for a week. The sky is orange and the air is unhealthy. You have not been told to leave.

prompts.ask: How do you know how bad the air is today?
ready: Knowing where to check the official air quality report
Knowing what its levels mean for the household
prompts.fix: A way to check the air quality and know what it means

prompts.ask: How do you keep the air inside cleaner?
ready: Everyone knows to keep windows and doors shut
An air cleaner, or a good filter in the heating or cooling
One room set up as a clean-air room
prompts.fix: A clean-air room, with an air cleaner or a good filter

prompts.ask: Someone has to go out. What do they wear?
ready: Well-fitting masks made for smoke
Everyone knows to keep trips short
prompts.fix: Masks made for smoke for the adults and older children they fit, and a plan to keep young children inside in the clean-air room

prompts.ask: Someone has asthma or a heart condition, or is very young or old. What changes for them?
ready: Their medicines and inhalers on hand
A plan for them to stay in the clean-air room
Knowing the signs that mean calling a doctor
prompts.fix: A plan for the people most at risk from smoke

prompts.ask: It is hot and the windows must stay shut. What now?
ready: A way to stay cool with the windows shut
Knowing a cooler public place to go
Plenty of water to drink
prompts.fix: A way to stay cool with the windows shut

prompts.ask: What about the pets?
ready: A plan to keep pets indoors
Everyone knows to keep walks short
prompts.fix: Keep pets inside when the air is bad

prompts.ask: The fire moves toward you and an alert says be ready to leave. What do you do?
ready: Go-bags ready by the door
The car fuelled
Routes and a place to go agreed
Everyone knows to leave as soon as officials say so, without waiting
prompts.fix: Be ready to leave: go-bags, fuel, routes and a place to go

scenarios.name: An earthquake
scenarios.setting: A strong earthquake hits in the early evening while everyone is at home. The shaking lasts less than a minute.

prompts.ask: The ground starts to shake. What does everyone do?
ready: Everyone has practised drop, cover and hold on
Anyone in a wheelchair or using a walker has practised lock, cover and hold on
Everyone knows to stay inside, away from windows
Everyone knows the safe spot in each room
prompts.fix: Practise drop, cover and hold on in each room

prompts.ask: The shaking stops. What first?
ready: A plan to check everyone for injuries
Shoes by each bed, because of broken glass
Flashlights by each bed, and everyone knows not to light candles or flames after a quake
prompts.fix: Shoes and a flashlight by each bed

prompts.ask: You smell gas. What do you do?
ready: Everyone knows to leave the home at once if they smell gas
Everyone knows not to turn the gas off as practice
Everyone knows not to use switches, flames or anything that can spark
Someone knows where the gas shutoff is, knows to turn it off only if there is a smell or a hiss and it is safe to reach, and knows that only the gas company turns it back on
The gas emergency number for where you live written down, to call from outside, away from the home
prompts.fix: Know where the gas shutoff is and when to turn it off, but never turn it off to practise

prompts.ask: Is the home safe to stay in?
ready: Knowing what damage to look for: cracks and fallen things
Everyone knows to leave if the home looks unsafe
Tall furniture fixed to the walls ahead of time
prompts.fix: Tall furniture and shelves fixed to the walls

prompts.ask: An aftershock hits. What do you do?
ready: Everyone knows to drop, cover and hold on again
Everyone knows to stay away from damaged parts of the home
prompts.fix: Expect aftershocks and practise again

prompts.ask: Phone lines are busy. How do you reach family?
ready: Everyone knows to send texts rather than call
An out-of-area contact everyone checks in with
A meeting place for anyone who is out
prompts.fix: An out-of-area contact everyone texts, and a meeting place

prompts.ask: The tap water may not be safe. What do you drink?
ready: Stored drinking water
Knowing how to make water safe to drink
prompts.fix: Stored water, and a way to make water safe

scenarios.name: A week with no running water
scenarios.setting: A water main breaks. The taps run dry, and a notice says it may be a week before water comes back.

prompts.ask: The taps stop. What do you do first?
ready: Knowing the official source that says how long
A plan to use stored water with care
Knowing to turn the taps off so nothing floods when water comes back
prompts.fix: Know where to find official notices about the water

prompts.ask: How much water do you have, and how will it last?
ready: Stored drinking water for everyone, pets included
Knowing where water will be handed out
prompts.fix: Stored drinking water for everyone, pets included

prompts.ask: How do you use the toilet?
ready: Strong bags and a bucket as a toilet
Knowing a way to get rid of waste safely
prompts.fix: A plan for toilets with no running water

prompts.ask: How do you keep hands and dishes clean?
ready: Soap and some stored water to wash hands after the toilet and before food
Hand sanitiser for when hands are not visibly dirty
Wipes
Paper plates and cups
prompts.fix: Soap and stored water for washing hands, hand sanitiser, wipes and paper plates

prompts.ask: What do you eat?
ready: Food that needs little or no water
A can opener that works by hand
prompts.fix: Food that needs little or no water

prompts.ask: Water comes back with a notice to boil it. What do you do?
ready: Everyone knows to follow the notice: boil water as it says, or use stored water
Everyone knows to drink tap water only when told it is safe
A plan to store water again
prompts.fix: Know what to do when a boil notice is given

scenarios.name: A medical emergency at home with phones down
scenarios.setting: Phone and internet service are down in the area. In the evening, someone at home falls and is badly hurt.

prompts.ask: What do you do first?
ready: Someone here has learned first aid on a course, including how to check breathing
Someone here has learned how to stop heavy bleeding
Someone here has learned CPR
Everyone knows: do not move someone whose neck or back may be hurt unless they are in danger where they are
prompts.fix: Someone here learns first aid and CPR on a first aid course

prompts.ask: The phones do not work. How do you get help?
ready: Everyone knows to try the emergency number anyway
Someone has checked ahead whether texting the emergency number works where you live, since in many places it does not or you must sign up first
Knowing which neighbour may have a working phone or radio
Knowing where the nearest place to get help is, like a fire station or police station
prompts.fix: Know how to reach help with the phones down: a neighbour, and the nearest place to get help

prompts.ask: Someone has to go for help while another stays. Who goes, where do they go, and what do they say?
ready: The household has agreed who goes for help and who stays with the person
The one who goes is an adult
The one who goes knows to say the address, what happened, how the person is and what has been done
The address and directions to the home are written down for whoever goes
Someone stays with the children and pets
prompts.fix: Know who goes for help, where to go, and what to say

prompts.ask: Help is on the way. What does the household do while you wait?
ready: Someone stays with the person the whole time
Everyone knows to keep the way in clear and leave a light on so helpers can find the home
Someone watches for the helpers and shows them in
prompts.fix: Know what each person does while waiting for help

prompts.ask: Where is the first aid kit, and what is in it?
ready: A first aid kit is where everyone can find it
The kit is checked and restocked, with gloves, dressings and tape
prompts.fix: A stocked first aid kit that everyone can find

prompts.ask: A helper asks about the person's medicines and allergies. Who knows?
ready: Each person's medicines and allergies written down
Kept with the first aid kit or in the household plan
prompts.fix: Each person's medicines and allergies written down

prompts.ask: How do you tell family what happened?
ready: An out-of-area contact
Numbers written on paper
prompts.fix: Numbers written on paper, and an out-of-area contact
